transcript:
Header: 2026-03-18 15:00 PST | Duration: 52m
Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Camille Ortiz (CS), Maya Chen (Aurora - Procurement), Liam Ortega (Aurora - Security), Sofia Alvarez (Aurora - Platform), Ethan Park (Aurora - Legal)

[00:00] Jordan Lee: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, we'll kick off - uh - this is Jordan from Redwood, with Priya and Camille. Thanks for making time.
[00:08] Maya Chen: Hi, thanks, Maya here. We got a short agenda, procurement plus legal asks, SLAs and pricing for the Dedicated offering.
[00:15] Priya Nair: Quick intro from me, I'll run the technical bits and the trial setup.
[00:22] Liam Ortega: Liam here; security questions up front: SOC2, data residency, KMS, audit logs.
[00:28] Jordan Lee: Totally, we'll cover those. First, do you want to run through procurement timeline, Maya?
[00:34] Maya Chen: Sure. We're aiming to finalize vendor selection by end of month, internal approvers are procurement then legal then VP ops. We need MSA + DPA with redlines in two business days ideally.
[00:44] Jordan Lee: Understood. We can get a redline back by Friday. We'll include our standard SLAs and dedicated capacity options.
[00:51] Ethan Park: Quick note, legal will be focused on indemnity, data processing terms, and liability caps. We'll need to see DPA specifics on subprocessors and data deletion.
[01:02] Priya Nair: On subprocessors, Redwood lists our infra providers in the appendix; we support customer-managed KMS for Private and Dedicated deployments and can provide logs.
[01:12] Liam Ortega: Can you confirm KMS integration for Dedicated in VPC? Also key rotation and HSM support?
[01:18] Priya Nair: Yes, Dedicated supports BYOK via our KMS integrations; HSM depends on the deployment partner but we do support standard HSM-backed KMS in our Private deployments. I'll put the architecture diagram in the follow-up.
[01:28] Jordan Lee: Pricing side - Maya, is Aurora looking at committed capacity or pay-as-you-go?
[01:33] Maya Chen: Committed for predictability. We'll need committed monthly GPU hours and a pricing table. Also a provision for burst capacity.
[01:42] Jordan Lee: Great. We have Reserved Capacity blocks with burst credits; we'll include a sample 12-month commit, discount tiers, and an early-termination clause.
[01:52] Sofia Alvarez: For the trial, we want to run a throughput test with our 6k token seq baseline and some low-latency chat flows. Can you guarantee baseline latencies?
[02:03] Priya Nair: We'll do a benchmark in the trial Dedicated environment - our telemetry gives per-route latency SLOs; we can set expectations, e.g., p95 latencies for the model family. We'll need your test prompts and traffic pattern.
[02:13] Sofia Alvarez: I'll share a synthetic workload and a small sample of production prompts.
[02:18] Jordan Lee: Perfect. Anything else on SLAs? We offer SLA tiers on uptime with credits and optional higher-tier SLOs for Dedicated.
[02:26] Maya Chen: On liability caps, can you confirm if the cap is tied to annual fees? That's what our legal usually asks.
[02:32] Jordan Lee: Standard wording ties liability cap to fees paid in last 12 months; we can discuss exceptions. We'll highlight that in the redline.
[02:40] Ethan Park: Also need to confirm breach notification timelines and incident response commitment.
[02:45] Priya Nair: Incident playbooks and SOC2 audit cadence will be attached. For breach notification we meet typical 72-hour windows for confirmed incidents - we can discuss stricter timelines in the redline.
[02:55] Liam Ortega: On data residency: we need EU-only residency for a subset of workloads. Can Dedicated be pinned to a specific region?
[03:03] Priya Nair: Yes, Dedicated capacity can be provisioned in region and we support routing policies. For Private deployments we can do customer-managed on-prem. We'll note regional pinning options.
[03:11] Maya Chen: Good. On the DPA, our privacy team will ask about subprocessors and standard contractual clauses. Do you support SCCs?
[03:18] Jordan Lee: Yes, we can include SCCs or equivalent contractual protections. We'll include a DPA template with that.
[03:24] Sofia Alvarez: About telemetry - will you provide token-level cost and latency breakdowns? We need to attribute costs to product teams.
[03:31] Camille Ortiz: Yes, Redwood Console gives token-level breakdowns per-route and per-model, and we can export usage reports. We'll attach sample console screenshots.
[03:39] Maya Chen: Procurement will want an onboarding checklist and a runbook for our infra team.
[03:44] Priya Nair: We'll provide onboarding checklist: account setup, VPC peering, KMS, RBAC, test data, and can schedule a 2-week runbook-led trial.
[03:53] Ethan Park: Any third-party pen test or attestation? We may require penetration test results or allow a vendor questionnaire.
[03:59] Jordan Lee: We have external pen test summaries and can fill vendor security assessment questionnaires. Priya will include the questionnaire responses.
[04:07] Liam Ortega: Logging retention and SIEM integration - can you push logs to our Splunk?
[04:12] Priya Nair: Yes, we support log forwarding via secure endpoints and can provide event streams for audit logs, with configurable retention.
[04:20] Maya Chen: Timeline recap - we need redline + DPA by Friday, internal legal review next week, and final sign-off by end of month. Is that feasible?
[04:29] Jordan Lee: Yes, we can do redline by Friday. We'll aim to have security artifacts by Thursday.
[04:35] Sofia Alvarez: For the trial, how quickly can you stand up Dedicated nodes?
[04:40] Priya Nair: Usually 3-5 business days for a Dedicated trial environment once we have the acceptance form and baseline capacity defined. If you need faster, we can use hosted with routing policy to mimic latency but won't be dedicated.
[04:53] Maya Chen: Procurement: we need pricing for a 12-month commit and a month-by-month option for comparison.
[04:59] Jordan Lee: We'll send both options. Also include overage pricing and burst credits.
[05:06] Ethan Park: Contract clause on data deletion - need confirmation on data purge timelines post-termination.
[05:11] Priya Nair: Standard is 30 days for hosted and Dedicated; for Private we follow customer-controlled retention. We'll note options for faster purge if required.
[05:20] Liam Ortega: For encryption at rest, is it AES-256 and are keys customer-managed?
[05:26] Priya Nair: AES-256 is standard; customer-managed KMS is available on Dedicated/Private. We'll document key lifecycle and rotation.
[05:34] Jordan Lee: Ok let's move to next steps - recap and responsibilities.
[05:38] Jordan Lee: Jordan to send redlined MSA and DPA, Priya to attach SOC2/ISO summary and network diagram, Camille will provide onboarding checklist and sample pricing, Maya to confirm procurement timeline and approvers, Sofia to provide workload samples for benchmarking, Ethan to review DPA and send legal comments.
[05:58] Maya Chen: Sounds good. One more question - are there any blackout windows for maintenance? We need maintenance schedule for Dedicated.
[06:06] Priya Nair: Maintenance windows are planned and we give 72-hour notice for non-critical maintenance; emergency maintenance may be sooner but we have fallbacks and can set blackout windows in the contract for critical services.
[06:18] Sofia Alvarez: Regarding fallbacks - if a model variant is unhealthy do you auto-failover to a compatible model? How transparent is that routing?
[06:27] Priya Nair: We have smart routing and automatic fallback to compatible variants; it's configurable and visible in the Console. We'll demo that in the trial.
[06:35] Ethan Park: Legal will look at indemnity for model outputs; we may request carveouts or specific language.
[06:41] Jordan Lee: Noted; we'll flag that area in the redline.
[06:45] Maya Chen: Okay, thanks. We'll expect the documents and security artifacts.
[06:49] Jordan Lee: Thanks everyone - we'll follow up with the redline and attachments, and propose times for the legal call. Appreciate the time.
[06:55] (meeting ends)

Notes: transcription had some auto-corrections: e.g., "BYOK" was sometimes transcribed as "B Y O K"; occasional speaker mislabels. Links shared: /redwood/attachments/MSA-Redline-2026-03-18.pdf (to be sent), /redwood/security/SOC2-summary.pdf, /console/screenshots/usage-breakdown-sample.png
